plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Streets and parks in the southern hemisphere late spring turn into rivers of lavender-blue as thousands of trumpet-shaped blossoms open on feathery, fern-like trees. When the petals fall, they carpet the pavement in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and across southern Africa, Australia and South America
plants.funFact: Although jacaranda is native to South America, Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of street trees.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub brightens late autumn gardens with delicate, silky blooms. They are often lightly fragrant and open when most other plants have finished for the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southern Japan, where it is native, and gardens in the southeastern United States and Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which is used in cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Wild poinsettias grow into tall, lanky shrubs lit by fiery red bracts, which are leaves that look like petals. They surround small yellow flower clusters, and the display glows through the dry season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere), triggered by long nights
plants.location: Southern Mexico, its native range, and warm gardens in places such as California and Florida
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used its sap and bracts for dye and medicine. Its flowering depends on long, uninterrupted nights, which is why it blooms near the winter solstice.
